rows.deadline: Immediately by e-mail; in writing within 7 days
rows.quote: The marketing authorisation holder and local representaive shall monitor the data generated while the study is being conducted and consider their implications for the risk-benefit balance of the medicinal product concerned. Any new information that may affect the risk-benefit balance of the medicinal product shall be communicated immediately via email and in writing within 7 days to the Board. Information affecting the risk-benefit balance of the medicinal product may include an analysis of adverse reactions and aggregated data.

f.title: PAES: report individual ADR cases and summarise AEs in interim and final reports
f.statement: For PAES, individual cases of suspected adverse reactions should be reported to the Board, and AEs/ADRs collected in studies with primary data collection should be recorded and summarised in the interim safety analysis and the final study report.
f.applicability: Post-authorisation safety studies conducted in Sierra Leone.

f.title: PAES: put AE collection and reporting procedures in the protocol; use the Board or a CIOMS-compliant form
f.statement: Procedures for the collection, management (including MAH review if appropriate) and reporting of suspected adverse reactions/events should be put in place and summarised in the PAES protocol. Reports can use the Board's ADR form or in-house forms that contain all required data elements, are readable and comply with the CIOMS I format.

f.title: PAES: submit quarterly progress reports within 21 days in the Board format
f.statement: The PAES progress report documents study progress (e.g. patients entered or exposed, outcomes, problems and deviations) and should be submitted in the Board-approved format (Appendix 11) within 21 days after the end of each quarter, counted from the study start date.
f.applicability: Post-authorisation safety studies conducted in Sierra Leone.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder or local representative
rows.deadline: Within 21 days after the end of each quarter from study start
rows.quote: The progress report is meant to include relevant information to document the progress of the study, for example, the number of patients who have entered the study, the number of exposed patients or the number of patients presenting the outcome, problems encountered and deviations from the expected plan. The progress report should be submitted in the Format approved by the Board (please refer to appendix 11). Progress report should be submitted within 21 days after the end of the preceding quarter. The quarter starts from the study start date.

f.title: Submit the DSUR annually, within 60 days of the DSUR data lock point based on the DIBD
f.statement: The DSUR should be submitted to the Board by the sponsor no later than 60 days after the DSUR data lock point, which should be the last day of the one-year reporting period; the annual period starts on the month and date of the Development International Birth Date (the sponsor's first authorisation to conduct a clinical trial anywhere).
f.applicability: Medicinal products marketed in Sierra Leone (PBSL guide PBSL/GL/004).

rows.actor: Sponsor
rows.deadline: No later than 60 days after the DSUR data lock point
rows.quote: The DSUR should be submitted to the Board by the sponsor no later than 60 days after the DSUR data lock point. The data lock point of the DSUR should be the last day of the one-year reporting period. The “Development International Birth Date” (DIBD) is used to determine the start of the annual period for the DSUR. This date is the sponsor’s first authorisation to conduct a clinical trial in any country worldwide. The start of the annual period for the DSUR is the month and date of the DIBD.

f.statement: The DSUR should also include significant other findings pertinent to the safety of the investigational drug, including from observational or epidemiological studies, non-clinical studies, related DSURs, manufacturing or microbiological changes, and recently published literature.

f.title: Keep the DSUR concise and discuss all safety issues, without using it for initial notification
f.statement: A DSUR should be concise and show that the sponsor is adequately monitoring and evaluating the evolving safety profile; all safety issues found in the period should be discussed, but the DSUR should not be used for initial notification of significant new safety information or as the means of detecting new safety issues.
f.applicability: Medicinal products marketed in Sierra Leone (PBSL guide PBSL/GL/004).

f.title: Include relevant post-marketing study information in the DSUR
f.statement: Because clinical development often continues after approval, relevant information from post-marketing studies should also be included in the DSUR.

f.title: Use the full ICH E2F DSUR format, state non-applicable sections and consult the Board on eCTD placement
f.statement: The full ICH E2F format should be used for all DSURs; information should be concise and where none is available or a section does not apply this should be stated; a sponsor submitting in eCTD format should consult the Board on DSUR placement.
f.applicability: Medicinal products marketed in Sierra Leone (PBSL guide PBSL/GL/004).

f.title: State a directly accessible PSMF location (physical office address; electronic site)
f.statement: The required PSMF location information is a physical office address of the marketing authorisation holder; where the PSMF is held in electronic form, the location stated must be a site where the stored data can be directly accessed.
f.applicability: Medicinal products marketed in Sierra Leone (PBSL guide PBSL/GL/004).

f.statement: The note on significant audit findings and the associated corrective and preventive action(s) shall be documented in the PSMF until the CAPA has been fully implemented; the note is only removed once corrective action and/or sufficient improvement can be demonstrated or has been independently verified, and the addition, amendment or removal of notes must be recorded in the PSMF logbook.

f.title: Describe deviation management in the PSMF and document PV procedure deviations until resolved
f.statement: The PSMF should describe the process for recording, managing and resolving deviations from the quality system, and shall document deviations from pharmacovigilance procedures, their impact and management until resolved (e.g. as a list referencing the deviation report, its date and the procedure concerned).

f.statement: The PSMF annex shall contain: a list of written policies and procedures for complying with the Board's pharmacovigilance requirements; a list of contractual agreements covering delegated activities; a list of tasks delegated by the QPPV; a list of all completed audits for a period of five years and a list of audit schedules; and, where applicable, a list of performance indicators.

f.statement: Any non-compliance identified at a PBSL pharmacovigilance inspection should be addressed by the manufacturer's representative or marketing authorisation holder in a timely manner through implementation of a corrective and preventive action plan and submission of a compliance report.
